blockingIssues.description: The new input-routing tests exercise a mirrored `TestableInputRecordingHost` instead of `WinSwiftUIWindowHost.window(_:pointerMovedTo:)`, `window(_:mouseWheelAt:delta:)`, `window(_:keyDown:)`, and `windowDidLoseKeyboardFocus(_:)`, so VAL-CROSS-004/005/006 are still not proven through the production host seam.

`TestableInputRecordingRuntime` records events before delegating, and the assertions only inspect those recorder arrays, so the tests do not prove the real runtime consumed the dispatched pointer, wheel, keyboard, or focus-loss events.

The resize/DPI proof moved to a mirrored `TestableRuntimeObservingHost` instead of driving `WinSwiftUIWindowHost.window(_:didResizeTo:)`, so VAL-CROSS-003 still lacks end-to-end validation through the production host path.

The helper uses a test-only `surfaceDescriptor.scaleFactor` path, but production resize logic reads `window.scaleFactor`, which comes from `GetDpiForWindow(hwnd)`, so the DPI assertions do not cover the real seam.

The post-downgrade resize test only resizes the helper's frame renderer instead of proving the real same-session fallback path that reattaches the frame renderer, resizes it, and switches the active backend.

The timer observability seam is now real, but `testRefreshRateUpdatesControlRuntimeMinimumFrameInterval` still never drives a changed `monitorRefreshRate` through `WinSwiftUIWindowHost`, so VAL-CROSS-009 remains only partially proven.

The coalescing tests still stop at scheduling: they do not wait for the deferred reload task or assert `executedReloadCount`, reload completion, or render/present evidence, so queued reload execution is still unproven.

The dependency-filtering test never exercises the `ComponentHost` dependency-set rejection path, because manual `observe(...)` tokens are installed without populating `componentHost.observedObjects`, so VAL-CROSS-010 is still not validator-visible.

appliedUpdates.description: Added `.factory/library/host-runtime-test-seams.md` documenting that host resize uses `window.scaleFactor` from `GetDpiForWindow(hwnd)` and timer cadence uses `window.monitorRefreshRate`, so test-only surface-descriptor updates or output-only timer assertions do not prove the production seams.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: When hardening scrutiny evidence for host assertions, require tests to keep calling the real `WinSwiftUIWindowHost` methods under review rather than introducing mirrored helper hosts that duplicate production routing or resize logic.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Both `fix-input-routing-observable-assertions` and `fix-resize-dpi-propagation-test` replaced weak assertions with stronger checks gathered from test-only helper hosts, but the helpers bypassed the production `WinSwiftUIWindowHost` seams and left the original contract blockers unresolved.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Re-emphasize that the required `.factory/library/architecture.md` startup read still applies to narrow scrutiny-fix sessions, or document a deliberate exception if the mission wants to allow skipping it.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Both `fix-frame-path-render-after-batch-failure` and `fix-resize-dpi-propagation-test` skipped the required architecture-library read even though the skill currently lists it as a startup step.
